notes: Heading never man on man rather than never remains defensible; rule 69's generic-noun clause is followed here.

The unit boundary is also contestable: reading never as the realization of the clause negator ouk and man as a non-negative rendering of oudeis under rule 69 would make ouk aligned and leave the indefinite a bare noun. The accepted reading treats the whole negation as written in the indefinite and empties ouk under rule 41.
